newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah fluctuates in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah fluctuates in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah fluctuated against the dollar in late trading on Wednesday, dealers said.

One U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators were slightly biddish for the dollar following reports of a planned liquidation of several Indonesian banks this year which seemed to cause some nervousness in the market.
But dealers said it was shortlived and the rate stabilised in the afternoon as operators switched focus to weekend issues.
A private appraiser of financial institutions reportedly said that 57 banks would be liquidated while the licences of 50 others would be revoked this year because of mismanagement.
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said some 42 rural banks were in the process of being liquidated, but they did not involve commercial banks.
Spot rupiah closed at 2,362.30/62.60, compared with an opening of 2,362.60/63.10. Its low was 2,364.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,361.85/62.20 and 2,361.90/62.20, respectively.
The dollar-rupiah rate adjusted slightly higher in the morning on speculation of a higher central bank fixing.
But operators sold off dollars again after the central bank kept its fixing unchanged in the afternoon.
One local bank dealer said operators were also seen going for the rupiah because they wanted to enjoy weekend premiums.
Liquidity turned ample in the afternoon, with overnight money easing to some 10.0 percent. Overnight swap was at 0.4/0.5 and tom/next was quoted at 0.45/0.50 points.
One-month swap was at 13.25/13.75, two at 24.5/26.0, three at 38.0/38.5 and six at 76.5/78.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,362/2,554 and the conversion rate at 2,362/2,410 on Wednesday.
